I found no changelog entry saying a `wrangler r2 sql` or `wrangler pipelines` command was removed or moved. The results do show renamed flags and a deprecation path, plus the current R2 SQL command reference.

- **Flag renames in pipelines:** A Wrangler changelog entry lists renamed `wrangler pipelines create/update` flags, such as access-key-id becoming r2-access-key-id and transform becoming transform-worker. Rename wrangler pipelines <create|update> flags is the heading, and the entry is tied to PR #8012.
- **Legacy pipelines:** Pipelines created before September 25, 2025 through the legacy API are on a deprecation path. You can identify them in the dashboard or with the pipelines list command.
- **Current R2 SQL command:** The reference lists only one command, `wrangler r2 sql query`, which takes a warehouse name and a SQL query. R2 SQL is currently in open beta. R2 SQL expects there to be a WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable to be set. A newer preview version of the same page lists the same command, so nothing there suggests removal.
- **Pipelines setup:** The `wrangler pipelines setup` command now has a Simple mode that applies recommended defaults and automatically creates the R2 bucket and enables R2 Data Catalog if they do not already exist.

Gaps: the search didn't surface a changelog entry for removing or moving any `r2 sql` subcommand. For a definitive answer, check the workers-sdk wrangler CHANGELOG directly, since the results were mostly docs pages and PR fragments.

content.text:
As far as I can tell, they haven't gone anywhere. Cloudflare's current docs still list `wrangler r2 sql query <warehouse> "<SQL>"`, which needs the `WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN` env var. They also still list the `wrangler pipelines` commands (`setup`, `create`, `list`, and so on). I found no changelog entry removing or moving either one. Two changes might explain what you're seeing. Some `wrangler pipelines create/update` flags were renamed (for example, `--access-key-id` became `--r2-access-key-id`). Pipelines created before September 25, 2025 are now "legacy" and on a deprecation path. If the commands are missing for you, your Wrangler is probably too old. Run `npx wrangler@latest --version` to check, or upgrade.

Sources:
- [R2 SQL wrangler commands](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2-sql/reference/wrangler-commands)
- [Pipelines wrangler commands](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pipelines/reference/wrangler-commands/index.md)
- [Wrangler changelog](https://0294f77f.preview.developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/changelog/wrangler)
- [Legacy pipelines](https://41dd6664.previews.developers.cloudflare.com/pipelines/reference/legacy-pipelines/)
